title: Portable and Wireless Charging Solutions
desc: Understand power banks, wireless pads and shared charging kiosks: safety, standards, battery care and a simple service business.
outcomes: Explain how batteries, chargers and wireless pads work.
task: Test and compare three portable chargers, write a safety and quality note, and plan a small shared charging point with price and care rules.
condition: Three chargers (practice or real), a meter or phone app, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. No opening of battery packs.
standard: Capacity test is repeated and averaged; safety rules are followed; unsafe items are rejected; business plan shows costs; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Shop owners, repair techs, event hosts, students.
evidence: test table, safety note, price sheet, plan

quiz: Formula for Wh?
Volts x amp-hours. (Covered in module 1: Batteries and units. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Why losses?
Conversion and heat. (Covered in module 2: Wired charging standards. To pass that module: Entries correct.)
What marks safe goods?
Certification marks and protection circuits. (Covered in module 3: Wireless charging. To pass that module: Peer understands.)
What do you do with a swollen bank?
Isolate and dispose safely. (Covered in module 4: Testing capacity. To pass that module: Results recorded.)
Wireless pad efficiency issue?
Lower efficiency, more heat. (Covered in module 5: Safety and quality. To pass that module: Includes disposal.)
Why store at half charge?
Slows ageing. (Covered in module 6: Shared charging service. To pass that module: Costs and prices shown.)
How measure capacity?
Discharge into a known load and measure Wh. (Covered in module 7: Care and recycling. To pass that module: Rules specific.)
Why repeat tests?
To average errors. (Covered in module 8: Plan and review. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
Name a loss control.
Deposit. (Covered in module 8: Plan and review. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
Where recycle batteries?
Collection points. (Covered in module 8: Plan and review. To pass that module: Numbers real.)

ladder: Batteries and units

L1: learner can name charger parts. Focus module: Batteries and units (Understand, 3 h). mAh, V, Wh. Key points: Wh = V x Ah. A 10,000 mAh at 3.7 V is 37 Wh. Losses of 20 to 40% in conversion. Charge and discharge cycles age cells.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 37 Wh bank charges a 12 Wh phone about 2.5 times. Then set the activity: Calculate three examples. Mark against the standard: Maths correct. Check at this level: Formula for Wh? Model answer: Volts x amp-hours. Show examples.
Wired charging standards

L2: learner knows safety rules. Focus module: Wired charging standards (Understand, 3 h). Cables and speeds. Key points: Connector types and power delivery levels. Use quality cables; thin cables overheat. Match charger and device.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 65 W charger with the wrong cable charges slowly. Then set the activity: Make a compatibility table. Mark against the standard: Entries correct. Check at this level: Why losses? Model answer: Conversion and heat. Safety.
Wireless charging

L3: learner can calculate Wh. Focus module: Wireless charging (Understand, 3 h). Coils and fields. Key points: Pad and device must align. Efficiency is lower; more heat. Metal objects between can heat up.

Teach: open with the worked example. A wireless pad is 70% efficient, wasting 30%. Then set the activity: Explain how it works. Mark against the standard: Peer understands. Check at this level: What marks safe goods? Model answer: Certification marks and protection circuits. Sums.
Testing capacity

L4: learner can test a bank. Focus module: Testing capacity (Apply, 4 h). Measure, do not trust labels. Key points: Discharge fully into a known load and measure Wh. Repeat three times and average. Compare to the label.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 20,000 mAh bank delivers 55 Wh instead of 74 Wh claimed. Then set the activity: Test three banks. Mark against the standard: Results recorded. Check at this level: What do you do with a swollen bank? Model answer: Isolate and dispose safely. Test.
Safety and quality

L5: learner can compare devices. Focus module: Safety and quality (Evaluate, 4 h). Cheap packs can fail. Key points: Look for certification marks and protection circuits. Avoid swollen, hot or damaged units. Do not carry on aircraft against airline rules; check limits.

Teach: open with the worked example. A swollen bank is isolated in a safe container and disposed of properly. Then set the activity: Write a safety note. Mark against the standard: Includes disposal. Check at this level: Wireless pad efficiency issue? Model answer: Lower efficiency, more heat. Compare.
Care and recycling

L6: learner can run a kiosk team. Focus module: Care and recycling (Apply, 3 h). Extend life. Key points: Avoid heat; store at half charge. Recycle batteries at collection points. Repair only with trained people.

Teach: open with the worked example. A cafe has a labelled battery recycling box. Then set the activity: Write care rules. Mark against the standard: Rules specific. Check at this level: Why store at half charge? Model answer: Slows ageing. Team.
Plan and review
L7: learner can audit safety. Focus module: Plan and review (Create, 3 h). Pilot the idea. Key points: Run a one-week trial. Record use and complaints. Improve.

Teach: open with the worked example. Week one: 40 rentals, 2 losses; add deposit. Then set the activity: Present your review. Mark against the standard: Numbers real. Check at this level: How measure capacity? Model answer: Discharge into a known load and measure Wh. Peer audit.
